subthemes.name: Making distributed learning faster and fairer
subthemes.gist: When machine learning training spreads across many computers with different data, how do you keep progress fast and balanced? Papers tackle communication costs, unequal data distribution, and coordination.

subthemes.name: Finding the sweet spot in model tuning
subthemes.gist: Modern large models need fine-tuning to new tasks, but this is expensive. Papers ask: how can you adapt models with fewer computations and memory without losing quality?

subthemes.name: Handling noisy and uncertain information
subthemes.gist: Real-world data is messy with outliers and noise. How do optimization algorithms remain reliable when gradients are unreliable, data is heavy-tailed, or predictions are uncertain?

subthemes.name: Solving puzzles and planning problems
subthemes.gist: Combinatorial puzzles—routing, scheduling, assignment—are computationally hard. Can learning and neural methods find good solutions faster than traditional algorithms?

subthemes.name: Exploring without computing gradients
subthemes.gist: Some optimization problems don't allow gradient calculation (black-box functions, limited queries). How do algorithms work with only function values, simulations, or search?

subthemes.name: Balancing competing goals
subthemes.gist: Real problems have multiple objectives: accuracy, fairness, cost, speed. How do optimization algorithms find tradeoffs instead of optimizing just one goal?

subthemes.name: Understanding when and why optimization works
subthemes.gist: Gradient descent and neural network training have surprising behaviors. What are the mathematical principles and limits? Why does noise sometimes help? When do algorithms get stuck?

subthemes.name: Moving data across spaces and distributions
subthemes.gist: Sometimes data lives in different spaces (high-dimensional to low-dimensional, one distribution to another). How do you transport or transform it efficiently while preserving structure?

subthemes.name: Making predictions that know their limits
subthemes.gist: ML models should admit when they're uncertain. How do you quantify confidence, calibrate predictions, or provide guarantees that hold even on new data?

subthemes.name: Connecting neural networks and classical algorithms
subthemes.gist: Modern approaches unify neural learning with classical optimization methods (mirror descent, proximal, Newton). How do you combine their strengths for speed and reliability?
